title: Domain transition policy
description: A data-authored transition policy over a domain workflow: given the workflow's current state and the outcome an operation execution reported, it selects a DOMAIN ACTION from a CLOSED registry of named actions (EXECUTION-MODES.md D3) and moves to a next state. The action registry is the sole executable vocabulary — a policy may name ONLY a registered action name (see ActionName's enum) with typed, bounded parameters. It can NEVER name a Go function, a shell command, a service, or a file path: there is no free-form command/handler/exec/path field anywhere in this schema, and `additionalProperties:false` throughout means no such field can be smuggled in. This is what keeps data-authored policy from becoming arbitrary code execution. Domain code owns what each registered action DOES and its invariants; data only selects which legal action fires on which transition.

domain_kind.description: Which domain workflow this policy governs.

ActionName.description: The CLOSED registry of legal domain actions. Each name maps to one typed Go handler with declared invariants; a policy can select from this set and NOTHING else. Adding an action is a domain-code change that registers a new handler, never a data edit that invents a name.

PolicyTransition.description: One rule: in `from_state`, when the correlating operation reports `on_outcome` (or unconditionally when omitted), fire `action` with `params` and move to `to_state`.

on_outcome.description: Operation-contract outcome name that triggers this transition. Omit for an unconditional transition from the state.

operation.description: Optional operation id this rule is specific to (must be a registered operation-contract id). When set, the rule matches only when THAT operation reports the outcome; an operation-specific rule beats a generic (operation-less) rule at the same state+outcome. Omit for a rule that applies to any operation. Lets one workflow state route different completing operations to different actions (e.g. workshop-round completed -> open-review, workshop-finalize completed -> bind-plan) without conflating operation identity into the outcome vocabulary.

ActionParams.description: Typed, bounded parameters passed to the registered action handler. Keys are lowercase snake identifiers; values are JSON scalars only (string, number, integer, boolean) — never nested structures, and never a reference to code, a path, or a command. The handler interprets them; data never supplies behavior.
